## Last Verse
<!--Put a short poem you created using chatGPT of 20 to 30 lines,here!-->
I woke this morning to find a stranger in my bed,  
He wore my face, but something seemed misread.  
He moved when I moved, spoke when I spoke,  
Yet every word he uttered felt borrowed, every gesture a joke.  
The mirror recognized me; I did not recognize it.  
It offered no explanation, only an indifferent portrait.  
I raised my hand, and the stranger raised his too,  
As though we were both prisoners of something neither knew.  
Outside, the city carried on without a sound,  
The buildings leaned inward, the streets narrowed around.  
The people passed me with their familiar eyes,  
Each wearing a face I could not quite recognize.  
At noon, I received a letter from myself.  
It read: Your absence has been noted by the self.  
I was summoned to appear at half past three,  
Before a court that had no record of me.  
I arrived precisely, though I could not say where.  
A clerk asked my name; I told him I wasn't there.  
He searched through his papers, then quietly frowned:  
"Your existence, I'm afraid, cannot be found."  
I pleaded my case, but my voice came from the hall,  
And the man behind the desk was not a man at all.  
He stamped my papers, dismissed my appeal,  
And instructed me to report to the person I used to feel.  
By evening, the stranger had grown accustomed to me.  
He ate at my table, slept where I should be.  
I watched him extinguish the light with my hand,  
And wondered which of us was supposed to understand.  
Tomorrow, perhaps, I will wake and be whole.  
Or perhaps the stranger will inherit my soul.
